title: One-sided-error machines halt within the time bound
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be a language of binary strings, and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. If, on every input $x$, every branch halts within $T(|x|)$ steps, output $1$ has probability at least $2/3$ when $x\in L$, and every branch outputs $0$ when $x\notin L$, then every branch halts within $T(|x|)$ steps on every input.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet
$L$ is a language of binary strings
$T$ maps natural numbers to natural numbers
For every input, every branch halts within $T$ of its length
On members, output $1$ has probability at least $2/3
On nonmembers, every length-$T(|x|)$ choice word produces output $0$
